analysis: Excitatory postsynaptic potentials (EPSPs) are graded potentials that occur when neurotransmitters bind to receptors on the postsynaptic membrane, leading to depolarization. They are not all-or-nothing responses; instead, their amplitude can vary based on the amount of neurotransmitter released and the number of receptors activated. EPSPs can summate, meaning multiple EPSPs can combine to increase the likelihood of reaching the threshold for an action potential. They do not hyperpolarize the membrane; rather, they depolarize it. While they can spread passively along the membrane, they do not have a refractory period like action potentials do. Therefore, the most accurate statements regarding EPSPs are that they can be added (summation) and they can spread over distances, although the latter is more limited compared to action potentials.
